sources.title: Prince Gong's Mansion Travel Guide: Architecture, Gardens & History
sources.content:
Prince Gong's Mansion: Complete Text Content

Overview
Prince Gong's Mansion, also called Gong Wang Fu, represents one of the most exquisite examples of Qing dynasty architecture in Beijing. The site combines imperial elegance with accessible cultural experiences for modern visitors.

Historical Background
The mansion originated during the 18th century when a wealthy Qianlong-era official named Heshen commissioned its construction as a luxury residence. Following Heshen's execution, Prince Gong—the sixth son of the Daoguang Emperor—acquired the property. This prominent statesman became celebrated for diplomatic expertise and cultural patronage.

Throughout the late Qing period, the mansion hosted official ceremonies, political negotiations, and intellectual gatherings. After China's 1911 revolution, ownership changed multiple times. Modern restoration efforts have preserved the site as a museum.

Architectural Features
The complex follows classical courtyard-style design arranged along a central axis, separating official, family, and leisure spaces. Key structures include an ornate main reception hall featuring intricate wooden carvings and gilded embellishments, connected side halls, and covered walkways throughout.

Gardens & Landscaping
The gardens integrate winding pathways, ornate pavilions, reflective ponds, and carefully arranged rockeries according to classical Chinese principles. Water features and rock formations symbolize prosperity and stability.

Cultural Artifacts & Collections
The museum houses extensive Qing dynasty treasures including calligraphy, paintings, ceramics, lacquerware, and decorative arts from the 18th-19th centuries.

Visitor Information
Accessibility: Located near Beijing subway lines and major bus routes.
Timing: Early mornings or late afternoons offer quieter exploration; spring and autumn provide optimal weather.
Photography: Courtyards and pavilions offer varied composition opportunities; avoid flash in exhibition areas.

Suggested Itineraries
Half-Day: Central courtyard, main halls with artifacts, primary garden areas.
Full-Day: Extended guided tour of all halls, comprehensive artifact study, leisurely garden exploration.
Combined Visits: Pair with nearby Lama Temple or Beihai Park.

sources.title: Museums of Beijing #93: Prince Gong's Palace Museum
sources.content:
Museums of Beijing #93: Prince Gong's Palace Museum
The best house & garden in Beijing

Location: 17 West Qianhai Street, Xicheng District, Beijing. Nearest subway station is Beihai Bei Station, around ten minutes away on foot.
Opening: March 1st - Nov 15th 07:30-16:30, Nov 16th-Feb 28th 08:30-16:00
Cost: 30 RMB

The only Qing Dynasty mansion open to the public in Beijing, Prince Gong's Palace is a magnificent complex covering a huge 60,000 square metres in total, divided equally between the residence and the garden, both of which should be included on any visit here.

Very conveniently located for anyone spending time in the centre of Beijing, this site is on the south side of Houhai Lake, just a few minutes walk through some attractive hutongs.

Prince Gong's Palace Museum is actually one of the most popular tourist spots in Beijing, and in peak season can be exceptionally busy, so the recommendation is to go early. One visitor arrived at 08:30 and found it almost empty, but when leaving a couple of hours later tour groups were arriving.

Prince Gong himself was a Manchu nobleman in the later years of the Qing Dynasty. But this place wasn't actually built for him at all — it was constructed in 1777 for a man named Heshen, who has gone down in history as "the archetype of a flamboyantly corrupt official."

Heshen was executed after his benefactor, Emperor Qianlong, passed away, and his property was confiscated in 1799, to be handed to Prince Gong in 1851.

As the Qing Dynasty ended the mansion and grounds were gifted to the Catholic Church and used as a university until 1951. After this, the site was used for various purposes; people used it to live in, the Beijing Air Conditioning Factory took it over, and then finally, in 1982, it was taken back under state control.

The residence part is what the visitor arrives at first. A series of courtyards spread over a large area, each somewhat similar and each exceptionally pretty to look at. There are exhibits on various subjects spread around here (all with basically no English explanations provided, Chinese only).

While the mansion is interesting, it is the garden section which is truly most impressive. There is a small temple to the Dragon King where Prince Gong would give offerings. The emphasis on wealth here is omnipresent — one of the centrepiece places is a stelae with the Chinese character for wealth (fu) in the hand of Emperor Kangxi, and there is a lake shaped like a bat with trees around it which drop fruit into the water.

Entering the garden through the Western-style gate, a replica of one at the Summer Palace, or by climbing along the small replica Great Wall, the visitor is rewarded with lovely views of sculpted gardens, a small lake, multiple winding covered walkways, artificial hills, pagodas.

The very impressive Grand Theatre is in the garden area. At least two hours is needed to see the whole of the mansion and gardens. A strong recommendation exists for any visitor to Beijing.

sources.title: Prince Gong's Mansion (恭王府) - Beijing Official
sources.content:
Prince Gong's Mansion (恭王府) - Beijing Official

Prince Gong's Mansion is Beijing's largest and best-preserved Qing Dynasty princely mansion located at Qianhai Xijie to the north of Shichahai.

Built in the Qing Dynasty, it served as the residence of He Shen, a powerful minister during the reign of Emperor Qianlong. The mansion covers an area of 60,000 square meters and features traditional Chinese courtyards, pavilions, and gardens.

The mansion buildings are located in the south; the gardens are in the north and include several quadrangle courtyards, two-story buildings, and a grand Beijing opera house. The Grand Theater House in the eastern part of the garden features Beijing Opera, Kunqu Opera, and royal music performances daily.

In addition to the mansion, there is a 28,000-square-metre garden with 20 scenic spots, pavilions, artificial hills including rock from Lake Tai in Jiangsu, and ponds.

Admission: 40 yuan. Opening hours: 8:30-17:00 (stop ticketing at 16:10). Closed Mondays.

The 'Western-Style Gate,' the 'fu' Stele and the 'Grand Theater House' are referred to as the 'Three Uniqueness in Prince Gong's Mansion.'

Transportation: Take Subway Line 6 to Beihai North and leave from Exit B. Walk north along Sanzuoqiao Hutong for 5 minutes.

sources.title: Beijing Prince Gong Mansion (Gong Wang Fu) Travel Guide
sources.content:
Beijing Prince Gong Mansion Travel Guide

Prince Gong's Mansion is the largest and best-preserved Qing Dynasty princely mansion in Beijing. Covering an area of 60,000 square meters, it features traditional Chinese courtyards, pavilions, and gardens.

The mansion was constructed around 1777 and was originally the private residence of Heshen. Since November 1996, the buildings and gardens have become a tourist attraction.

Admission costs CNY 40, with opening hours from 8:30-17:00 (stop ticketing at 16:10). Closed Mondays.

The Three Uniqueness: Western-Style Gate, Grand Theater House, and the fu Stele.

Visiting Tips: Visit on a weekday and arrive when it first opens at 8:30 am. At least two hours is needed to see the whole mansion and gardens. Audio guide rentals available at Gate 2.

Free admission for children under 6 or under 1.2 meters. Half price for ages 7-18 and seniors over 60.

sources.title: 恭王府及花园 - 百度百科
sources.content:
恭王府及花园

基本信息
恭王府及花园是国家5A级旅游景区，位于北京市西城区前海西沿、什刹海南岸。这是清代规模最大的一座王府，占地约6万平方米（花园2.8万平方米）。

历史沿革
乾隆四十九年（1784年），和珅建造此府。嘉庆四年（1799年）正月，和珅获罪赐死抄家，宅邸赐予庆王永璘。咸丰二年四月（1852年6月），奕䜣正式移居此府，府名史称恭王府。

民国时期：1912年溥伟从恭王府出逃。1937年受圣言会委托，恭王府被购得用于辅仁大学女院。

新中国成立后：周恩来是第一人提出保护恭王府的。1982年被国务院公布为第二批国家重点文物保护单位。1988年8月17日花园对外开放，2008年8月20日府邸对外开放。

建筑特点
选址：恭王府位于北京城的"水龙脉"上，处于"龙腹之穴"。风水学认为水象征财富，使其成为"北京城最有财气的地方"。

结构：府邸分为中、东、西三路建筑，各由多进四合院组成。中路的3座建筑是府邸的主体，一是大殿，二是后殿，三是延楼。延楼东西长160米，有40余间房屋。

花园名为萃锦园，建于乾隆四十二年（1777年）。

主要建筑
银安殿：俗称银銮殿，王府最主要建筑。民国十年因烧香失火被毁，现为复建。
嘉乐堂：和珅时期之建筑，恭亲王时期作为王府祭祀场所。
后罩楼（藏宝楼）：长180多米，为国内王府类建筑中最长的楼。后墙有44个什锦窗，每个图案不同。
锡晋斋（楠木殿）：金丝楠木的室内装潢，用料考究，耗资巨大。
多福轩：恭亲王时期的穿堂客厅，殿前有长了两百多年的藤萝。
乐道堂：恭亲王奕䜣的起居处。

花园部分
西洋门：位于花园中路最南端，是花园的正门。门由汉白玉石雕砌，形制仿圆明园中大法海园门所建，西洋拱式风格。恭王府的三绝之一。
独乐峰：高约5米的北太湖石孤赏石。
蝠池：因形似蝙蝠而得名，有祈福的寓意。
安善堂：萃锦园中路最主要建筑，为恭亲王宴请重要宾客之处。
滴翠岩：由太湖石叠成的宝嵎。
福字碑：位于秘云洞内，由清圣祖康熙皇帝的御笔刻成。这块碑石长7.9米，贯穿整座假山。
蝠厅（蝠殿）：位于花园中路最北端，形制多变，如蝙蝠两翼。彩绘斑竹全部是由油工一笔一笔画上的。
大戏楼：建于同治年间，是我国现存独一无二的全封闭式大戏楼。整个大戏楼虽为砖木结构建筑却没有用一根铁钉。

文化价值
恭王府被学者侯仁之称为"一座恭王府，半部清代史"。

福文化：府邸里有"多福轩"，花园前后有"蝠池、蝠厅"遥相呼应。恭王府建筑物的窗棂上、彩画上，蝙蝠的图案随处可见。

旅游信息
地址：北京市西城区前海西街17号
交通：地铁六号线北海北站B口出站
开放时间：8:30-17:00，16:10停止检票。周一闭馆。
门票：40元/人

sources.content:
北京恭王府最全游览路线及攻略

门票信息
门票价格：40元/人
系列游服务门票：70元（包括门票、专业讲解员、参观开放的景点及展厅）

优惠政策
离休干部凭离休证免费参观
6周岁以下（含6周岁）或身高1.2米以下儿童免费参观
残疾人免费参观
6周岁至18周岁未成年人、学生享受半价优惠

周二至周日 08:30-17:00（16:10停止售票），周一闭馆

预约购票
通过恭王府博物馆官网或公众号预约实名购票。最早可于参观十日前20:00开始预订。

推荐游览路线
宫门→银安殿→嘉乐堂→葆光室→锡晋斋（楠木殿）→后罩楼→西洋门→独乐峰→蝠池→安善堂→流杯亭→竹子院→牡丹园→怡神所→蝠厅→平步青云路→邀月台→滴翠岩→福字碑→方塘水榭→妙香亭→龙王庙→箭道→乐道堂→多福轩

交通指南
乘坐地铁6号线，在北海北站下车，从B东北口出站后，步行约10分钟即可到达恭王府。

sources.title: Prince Gong's Mansion, Prince Kung's Palace Museum, Gong Wang Fu
sources.content:
Prince Gong's Mansion, Prince Kung's Palace Museum

Prince Gong's Mansion is the largest princely mansion in Beijing, covering 60,000 square meters. It is a masterpiece of ancient Chinese architecture and garden design.

Historically, this was the residence of He Shen, a powerful minister during Emperor Qianlong's reign. The mansion was later passed to Prince Gong (Yixin), the sixth son of the Daoguang Emperor.

The Three Uniqueness: Western-Style Gate (仿圆明园的西洋建筑样式), Grand Theater House (全封闭式大戏楼), and the fu (福) Stele (康熙御笔福字碑).

The garden covers 28,000 square meters with 20 scenic spots. Key features include artificial hills with rock from Lake Tai, ponds, pavilions, the Bat Pool (蝠池), and winding pathways.

Admission: 40 yuan. Hours: 8:30-17:00. Closed Mondays.
Transportation: Subway Line 6 to Beihai North, Exit B, then walk 5 minutes north.
